title: Send Email with JavaMailSender
summary: Configure an SMTP connection, create a mail service, and understand sending failures.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: Send Email Using Spring Boot | Gmail SMTP | Java Mail Sender

richText: Send email through a mail server
SMTP is the protocol an application uses to submit email to a mail server.
JavaMailSender is Spring’s interface for sending email through that server.
Add spring-boot-starter-mail. Boot can create a JavaMailSender bean when the mail libraries and spring.mail.host are configured.
Use SimpleMailMessage for plain text. Use MimeMessage with MimeMessageHelper for HTML or attachments.
Spring Boot 3 uses Jakarta Mail types when you work directly with mail messages.
Configure the mail connection
The mail provider supplies the host, port, credentials, and encryption settings.
STARTTLS upgrades an existing connection to TLS. TLS encrypts the connection.
Keep credentials in environment variables or a secret store. Keep certificate validation enabled.
Set connection, read, and write timeouts so a mail call cannot wait indefinitely.

example.title: Configure authenticated SMTP with STARTTLS
description: This provider supports authenticated SMTP with STARTTLS on port 587.
Set MAIL_HOST, MAIL_USERNAME, and MAIL_PASSWORD in the environment. Add these settings to application.properties.
explanation: starttls.required rejects connections where the TLS upgrade cannot happen.
The three timeout values are in milliseconds. Each is five seconds.
Use your provider’s supported credentials. Gmail account policy may require an app password or OAuth.

sender.send submits the message to the mail server.
A sending failure raises MailException. Let it reach a caller that must retry or record failure.

richText: Submission and delivery are different
A successful send call means submission completed without a reported error. It does not guarantee delivery to the inbox.
The provider may later reject the message, return a bounce, or place it in spam.
Retry temporary failures with a limit. Invalid credentials or recipients need correction.
A timeout can happen after the server accepts the message. Retrying can submit it twice.
Store pending messages when sending must survive an application restart.
Send large batches through background work. Keep message bodies and recipient lists out of ordinary logs.
Authorize callers before allowing them to choose recipients or send private content.
